final.title: Pip and the Paper Moon
final.logline: Pip is a small index card that came to life. It digs a napkin idea out of a desk buried in terminals and sticky notes, and glues everything into one Claude Code console. From there Pip follows the idea through a day and a night: an agent gets briefed, the Scheduler works the job cards under a paper moon, files and memories get tidied, and a finished project page hangs on the showcase wall. Session Manager: build it, show it off, free and open.
final.mascot:
PIP is an original mascot: an index card that came to life. There is no Anthropic or Claude mark and no starburst, asterisk or sunburst shape anywhere in the film. Claude is only ever drawn as a plain cream speech-bubble window or a black paper terminal with a green crayon '> _'.
BODY: a 3:4 portrait rounded rectangle, about 150x200 px on a 1920x1080 stage, filled with butter construction paper #e4b85a using a rough.js hachure fill. It has a 2px ink #2a221a outline with a slight torn-edge wobble (jitter each outline vertex ±2px). Three faint ruled lines #e0d3b8 run across it, with one terracotta #b85c34 margin line down the left side. The top-right corner is dog-eared: a honey #d3a23c folded triangle about 30px on a side that acts as a cowlick and flops about 15° on every hop.
FACE, in the upper third: two mismatched googly eyes. They are white circles of radius 16 and 13 with a 2px ink outline, and each has a black pupil of radius 6 on a spring-damped offset (lag 0.15s, overshoot) that rattles when Pip stops. Below them is a crayon smile (one ink arc, 3px, rough) and two blush dots of radius 7 in #e8a988.
SCARF: a 14px strip of terracotta washi tape across the 'neck' (the lower third), striped diagonally in #e8a988 at 70% opacity, with two zig-zag torn tails that flutter on a sine wave.
LIMBS: two-segment pencil-stroke arms and legs in #5b4a36 (2.5px, rough), ending in sage #6f7d52 hole-punch dots of radius 6 for hands and feet.
ANTENNA: a bent paperclip polyline in hive-teal #4f7d72 topped with a butter dot of radius 7. At night the dot glows (radial gradient #e4b85a to transparent, radius 40) and becomes Pip's lantern.
PROPS: a stubby glue stick, a sage rectangle with a white rounded cap, which Pip thwacks to 'glue' pieces into place. Night costume: a navy paper nightcap (a triangle with a cream pom-pom circle).
MOTION: poses step at 15 fps like stop-motion, and the rough.js seed re-rolls about every 8 fps so outlines 'boil'. Squash and stretch on hops (scaleY 0.8 to 1.15), a ±3° idle wobble, and a 3px offset drop shadow of ink at 20% so Pip reads as a cutout lifted off the page.
PERSONALITY: eager, tidy-minded, a bit clumsy. Pip cheers, carries, points and tidies, but never starts work itself. A cut-out human hand or mitten finger always presses the buttons. Pip never speaks and reacts only through its eyes, cowlick and small doodle bubbles.
SUPPORTING CAST, all simple shapes: 'YOU' is a cut-out hand by day and a stick figure asleep in a paper bed at night. Job helpers are small sticky-note squares in sage, teal and #e8a988 with dot eyes and pencil legs. The agent trading cards are architect (triangle hard hat, blueprint roll), dev-lead (wrench) and validator (magnifying-glass circle).

final.musicDirection:
An original, whimsical 'kitchen-table orchestra' cue at 104 BPM in F major, 4/4. It should feel warm and handmade, never corporate or electronic. INSTRUMENTS: plucked ukulele, glockenspiel and toy piano on the melody, pizzicato bass, woodblock tick-tock, hand claps, plus kazoo and slide-whistle for comic accents. There is one short, hummable 4-bar motif.
ARC: 0–5.5s is comic chaos: detuned toy piano, off-beat kazoo honks and a clock ticking too fast, then one beat of silence on the tape-rip wipe. 5.5–18.5s: the main motif locks in (ukulele plus glock), with a pizzicato counterline for Agents. 18.5–25.5s: night lullaby, the motif on music box and felt piano over a warm pad at half-time feel, with near-silence on 'pauses'. 25.5s: sunrise glock glissando and the full band returns. 30.5–41s: light and bouncy (a toy-piano run on the airplane, a 'bwomp' on the crumple, a 'ding' on the basket shot). 41–48s: snare roll and doubled claps building to a hit on the push-pin. 48–54s: finale restatement, with a button ending (ukulele strum plus glock ding) at about 53s that rings out to silence.
Every page turn or swipe gets a short harp or glock swirl.
MIX: sidechain-duck the music about 10 dB under the VO and leave it unducked in the gaps. SFX are short and papery (rustles, tape rips, stamp thunks, pops, pins), sit about 6 dB under the voice, and are panned to where each prop is on screen.
FREE TOOLING: synthesize everything in web/promo-video/js/audio.js with WebAudio or Tone.js and render offline. Use Karplus-Strong plucks for the ukulele and pizzicato, sine plus a fast-decay bell envelope for glock and music box, a filtered-noise burst for rustles, swipes and tape rips, a low sine thump plus a noise click for stamps and pins, and a triangle oscillator with a fast LFO for the kazoo. If samples are used, take them only from CC0 sources (Freesound CC0, OpenGameArt CC0, FreePD).
VO: Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0) via tts/kokoro_say.py, with a warm, smiling voice (af_heart, or bf_emma for a storybook feel) at speed about 1.0 (about 140 wpm). Send 'bilko dot run' literally. Add 250–400 ms of breath at colons, dashes and full stops. Render one clip per scene and place it at scene start plus 0.15s. If a clip runs long, stretch that scene to the clip length plus 0.3s and shorten the end-card hold, keeping the total at 55s or less.
VO total: 112 words over 54s (about 124 wpm average; the fastest scenes, s2 and s8, run about 137 wpm).

---SCORES---
Each candidate is scored on charm, clarity across the 6 beats, accuracy, timing and animatability (out of 50).

A 'Once Upon a Desk' (Tuck): charm 9, clarity 8, accuracy 8, timing 6, animatability 9. Total 40.
- Charm: a lovely storybook frame, and the "happily ever after" close is great.
- Clarity: the showcase VO never mentions bilko.run.
- Timing: s2 runs 9s, over the 4–7s rule.
- Grafted from A: "Favorites become one-click buttons", the Hot keys button press, "Build… show off", and the broom-sweep energy (now Pip's glue stick).

B 'Scrap Glues It Together': charm 8, clarity 8, accuracy 7, timing 5, animatability 7. Total 35.
- Charm: the funniest hook.
- Accuracy: the pull-back implies the Project Home page is a collage of app features, but the real page covers what the project is, who it's for and how to run it. "Glues it into one console" was fine.
- Timing: s7 is 10s with 22 words, and s2 and s4 are 8s each.
- Animatability: assembling the pull-back is heavy.
- Grafted from B: the "Twelve terminals. Forty sticky notes." hook, "Claude arrives briefed" plus the AIM envelope under the Session door, the glue-stick prop, "like ours on bilko dot run", the ransom-note end card, and the chaos-to-groove music cut.

C 'Under a Paper Moon' (Pip), the WINNER: charm 9, clarity 9, accuracy 9, timing 6, animatability 8. Total 41.
- Clarity: the day/night arc makes the Scheduler concrete, and the idea threads through every scene.
- Accuracy: 'Needs you' is shown honestly, pause and resume are shown, the laptop is shown open with an 'app open = laptop stays awake' tag, and a human hand presses every button (single-creator law).
- Timing: s4 was 9s with 18 words, and the opening "one Session Manager" was weak.
- C supplied the spine, the mascot and the scene order.

SYNTHESIS FIXES:
- Every scene is now 4–7s and the timings are contiguous from 0 to 54s.
- The napkin idea is planted inside B's chaos hook, so it pays off in the architect's tear and the 'napkin-idea' tab.
- "While you sleep" became "Bedtime?", with the laptop visibly open.
- The showcase frames bilko.run as where the author's projects are showcased ("like ours"), not as a hosting service open to anyone.
- Clusters appear only after a button press.
- There is no Windows, Whisper, cloud, sandbox, paid-tier, 'Default' agent or swarm claim.
- Every VO line was re-checked against the verified facts.

drafts.title: Once Upon a Desk
drafts.logline: Once upon a desk, a tiny paper hedgehog named Tuck tidies a pile of scattered terminals into one cozy Claude Code console. Each turn of the storybook's pages shows another part of Session Manager: agents, bedtime to-do lists, files, memories, and finally your projects on show.
drafts.mascot: TUCK: an original palm-sized paper hedgehog who fusses cheerfully over a tidy desk. Tuck is never drawn with a radiating asterisk or starburst silhouette and never resembles any real logo. Tuck is built from 6 simple parts for canvas + rough.js. (1) BODY: an egg-shaped ellipse (about 1.3:1, wider than tall) of butter construction paper #e4b85a with a rough hachure fill and a 2px ink #2a221a outline. The bottom edge is slightly torn (a jagged polyline). (2) QUILLS: a half-fan of 7 colored-pencil quills along the back and top only. Each is a skinny sharpened pencil (long rectangle + small triangle tip with an ink dot), alternating terracotta #b85c34, honey #d3a23c and sage #6f7d52. They all angle backward like pencils in a cup and never radiate all the way round. (3) FACE: a pointed snout (a small triangle at the front of the body) ending in a round ink-black nose button. Two mismatched googly eyes (white circles, radius 9 and 11) have free-rolling black pupils that lag and wobble on every move. Two soft #e8a988 cheek circles. (4) FEET: two stubby kraft #efe6d3 ovals that flip-flop in a 2-frame waddle. (5) SCARF: a strip of translucent sage washi tape at the neck, with a zigzag torn end that flutters. (6) PROPS, swapped per scene: tiny broom (line + fan triangle), patchwork blanket (3x2 grid of colored squares), nightcap (triangle + pom-pom circle), matchbox bed, magnifying glass, round wire spectacles. MOTION: the whole figure 'boils', with the rough.js seed changing every 3 frames at 24fps (8fps line boil). Squash-and-stretch hop on entrances. Quills rattle (±4° jitter) when Tuck is excited. A 3px offset drop shadow in #5b4a36 at 25% makes Tuck look like a cutout lifted off the page. PERSONALITY: tidy-minded, a little smug, very huggable. Tuck never speaks and communicates only through expressions and small doodle thought-bubbles. NOTE: Claude itself is never drawn as a logo, only as plain cream speech-bubble windows with three typing dots, or black terminal windows with a green crayon prompt.

drafts.musicDirection: Whimsical storybook folk-pop, about 96 BPM, 4/4, F major. It should feel warm, cozy and handmade, never electronic or corporate. PALETTE: ukulele or nylon-string pluck, glockenspiel/celesta melody, pizzicato strings, upright-bass plucks, brushed snare and finger-snaps/hand-claps, plus kazoo or slide-whistle for the comic beats. STRUCTURE: music-box intro (0-2s) → wobbly pizzicato 'mess' bars with off-beat woodblocks (2-6.5s) → full theme when Tuck tidies (6.5s) → lighter variations on each page. Every page turn gets a short harp/glockenspiel glissando swirl. The Scheduler night (21.6-28.9s) is a lullaby breakdown: celesta and soft pad at half-time feel, with rubber-stamp SFX on the beat, then a bright ukulele pickup at sunrise. The music builds through Files and Memory, swells warmly for the Showcase (39.9-46.8s), then reprises the theme and ends on one sustained music-box note at about 53.5s. MIX: duck the music about 12 dB under the voiceover and keep SFX about 6 dB below the voice. VOICE: Kokoro TTS as a gentle bedtime-story narrator (e.g. bf_emma or af_heart), speed about 0.95. Leave a small beat after 'Then came Tuck' and before 'Session Manager'. If real TTS runs long, stretch each scene to its measured VO length plus about 0.4s, capped at 55s total. FREE SOURCING: everything can be synthesized in the browser with Tone.js/Web Audio and rendered offline (Tone.Offline or MediaRecorder). Use PluckSynth for the ukulele, FMSynth/MetalSynth bells for the glockenspiel and music box, and filtered NoiseSynth bursts for paper rustles, stamps, swipes and page flips. Alternatively, use a CC0/royalty-free bed from Pixabay Music and CC0 SFX from Freesound.

Draw it as one irregular 7–9 point polygon, redrawn with rough.js each frame at a small random offset so the torn edge 'boils' (about 8 fps), with a slightly lighter torn-fiber stroke (#fbf6ec) along one edge. Below them is a tiny crayon smile, a single arc. On its 'neck' sits a strip of terracotta washi tape (#b85c34) with faint diagonal stripes that works as a bandana, one tail flapping. Its arms and legs are single wobbly pencil lines (#5b4a36) ending in little loops for hands and feet. Prop: a stubby glue stick (a sage #6f7d52 rectangle with a white rounded cap). Scrap slaps it down to 'glue' each piece into place. Personality: earnest, tidy-minded and a bit clumsy. When it's surprised its eyes spin, and when it's happy its edge flutters like paper in a breeze. It has no text, logo or letterforms on its body, and it looks nothing like Anthropic's or Claude's mark.

drafts.musicDirection: Whimsical, warm, handmade feel, about 112 BPM in F major, all synthesizable for free in Web Audio / Tone.js: a Karplus-Strong plucked 'ukulele', sine+triangle bell 'glockenspiel', pizzicato made from short filtered saw plucks, soft brushed kick plus a noise shaker, and hand claps from filtered noise bursts. drafts.title: Under a Paper Moon
drafts.logline: Pip, a small index-card mascot, follows one idea through a day and a night. In the morning it's a doodle on a napkin. An agent tears it into job cards, and the Scheduler works through them under a paper moon while you sleep. At sunrise there's a pile of finished work, a Memory corkboard you can tidy, and a Project Home portrait to pin on the wall. It all happens in Session Manager, one free and open console for Claude Code.
drafts.mascot: PIP, an index card that came to life. It is ORIGINAL: no Anthropic or Claude mark, and no starburst, asterisk or sunburst shape anywhere in the film. BODY: a 3:4 portrait rounded rectangle about 150x200 px on the 1920x1080 stage, cut from butter construction paper (#e4b85a) with a torn-edge wobble on the outline. Faint ruled lines (#e0d3b8) cross the body, with one terracotta margin line (#b85c34) down the left side. The top-right corner is dog-eared: a honey (#d3a23c) folded triangle that works as a cowlick and flops on every hop. FACE: two mismatched white googly eyes (radius 16 and 13) whose black pupils lag behind body motion on a spring and rattle when Pip stops. A crayon-scribble smile in ink (#2a221a) and two rosy cheek dots (#e8a988). SCARF: a strip of terracotta washi tape with diagonal stripes in accent-muted #e8a988, wrapped at the "neck", with two fluttering tails. LIMBS: 2-segment pencil-stroke stick arms and legs in ink, ending in round paper-punch dots in sage (#6f7d52) for hands and feet. ANTENNA: a bent paperclip line in hive-teal (#4f7d72) topped by a round butter "glow dot". At night the dot lights up (a soft radial glow) and Pip carries it like a lantern. NIGHT COSTUME: a navy paper nightcap (a triangle with a round pom dot). MOTION RULES: pose on 15 fps stop-motion steps, and re-seed rough.js lines every ~7.5 fps so outlines "boil". Squash and stretch on hops, a ±2-3° idle wobble, and a 2 px offset paper drop-shadow (ink at 20%). PERSONALITY: an eager, slightly clumsy helper. Pip cheers, carries, points and tidies, but never starts work itself. A cut-out human hand always presses the buttons. SUPPORTING CAST, all simple shapes: (1) "YOU", a cut-out hand by day and a stick figure asleep in a paper bed at night. (2) Claude jobs as small square sticky-note helpers in sage, teal and accent-muted, with two dot eyes and pencil legs, left unbranded. (3) Agent trading-card figures: architect (hard-hat triangle, blueprint roll), dev-lead (wrench), validator (magnifying-glass circle).

drafts.musicDirection: An original, whimsical "kitchen-table orchestra" cue at 104 BPM in F major. Instruments: plucked ukulele, glockenspiel and toy piano on melody, pizzicato bass, a woodblock tick-tock, hand claps and one kazoo accent. There is one short, hummable 4-bar motif. ARC: 0–17.5 s is the bright A theme. 17.5–26.5 s is the night lullaby: the same motif on music box and felt piano over a warm pad, with soft crickets. At 26.5 s the sunrise lifts with a glock glissando and the full band returns. 41–48 s builds with a snare roll and doubled claps. 48–54.5 s is the finale hit, with a button ending (ukulele strum plus glock ding) at about 53.5 s that rings to silence. MIX: duck the music about 10 dB under the VO with a sidechain on the VO bus. SFX sit just under the VO and are panned to where each prop is on screen. FREE TOOLING: synthesize everything in the existing web/promo-video/js/audio.js with WebAudio. Use Karplus-Strong plucks for ukulele and pizzicato, sine plus a fast-decay bell envelope for glock and music box, a filtered-noise burst for paper rustle and tape rip, a low sine thump plus a noise click for stamps and pins, and a triangle oscillator with a fast LFO for the kazoo. If samples are wanted instead, use only CC0 sources (Freesound CC0, OpenGameArt CC0, FreePD). VO: use Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0) through tts/kokoro_say.py, with a warm, smiling voice (e.g. af_heart) at speed ~1.0 (about 140 wpm). Write the URL as "bilko dot run" in the text sent to TTS. Add 250–400 ms of breath at colons and full stops. Render one VO clip per scene and place each at its scene start plus about 0.15 s.

pillars.name: Scheduler
pillars.oneLiner: Hand Claude a to-do list before bed: Session Manager breaks work into small written job cards, runs them one after another as background Claude jobs while you sleep, checks each one's work, and leaves a queue that shows what's done and what needs you.
userFacingNames: Start jobs: when available / on-reset / manual
Nothing to run yet — the scheduler needs a session.
verifiedFacts: The scheduler runs queued PRDs (markdown work orders) as headless `claude -p` jobs (src/main/scheduler.cjs:1-3; session-manager-operations/scheduler/README.md:111-113)
Every job spawn passes `--model` explicitly, plus `--output-format stream-json` and `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (src/main/scheduler.cjs:5438-5448)

A PRD's `agentType` picks a persona whose body is passed as `--append-system-prompt` and whose `model` field becomes `--model`, falling back to `sonnet` (session-manager-operations/scheduler/README.md:54-62; src/main/lib/agentModelResolve.cjs:38)

PRDs are markdown files stored per Epic under `session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/<epic-id>/prds/`, and each job's status is one of pending / running / completed / failed / needs_review (session-manager-operations/scheduler/README.md:11-14, 70-76)
When a PRD finishes it moves to `prds-archived/` so it can't be run again, and every run is appended to `state/history.jsonl` (session-manager-operations/scheduler/README.md:114-117)

`dependsOn` orders jobs: the picker only launches a pending row once its dependsOn chain is satisfied, and the UI's 'Ready now' cell counts 'Pending rows whose dependsOn chain is fully satisfied right now' (src/main/lib/schedulerBatch.cjs:479-486, 128; src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/SchedulerTopBands.tsx:380-386)

One machine-wide slot pool caps concurrent `claude -p` processes: default 5, ceiling 10, adjustable in the UI, and shared by scheduler jobs and chat runs (src/main/lib/sessionSlots.cjs:34-35; session-manager-operations/scheduler/README.md:99-103; src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/SchedulerTopBands.tsx:454)

The default start policy is 'when-available': jobs start whenever usage in the tightest Claude billing window is under 90%. 'on-reset' (legacy) and 'manual' (Run now only) are the alternatives (src/main/scheduler.cjs:998-1008, 8635-8654)

When a job hits a rate limit the scheduler pauses itself and sets a resume timer, which clears the pause and runs due jobs at reset. A manual pause never auto-resumes (src/main/scheduler.cjs:5956, 3904-3935)

First-run guide copy: 'Jobs start themselves inside your window, pause on rate-limit, and resume at the reset. History records how each ended.' (src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/FirstRunGuide.tsx:15-16)

The app blocks system suspend while it's open so scheduler polling and `claude -p` jobs 'survive an idle laptop' (Electron powerSaveBlocker, plus a systemd-inhibit backstop on Linux) (src/main/index.cjs:110-120, 1450-1461)
README pitch: 'queue overnight work as PRDs' (README.md:7)

Each job runs in its own `git worktree` on a `sm-job/<slug>` branch, so concurrent jobs don't trample each other or the user's own session. Its edits, test runs and commit stay isolated until integration (src/main/lib/jobWorktree.cjs:1-21; src/main/lib/gitWorktree.cjs:88-96)

Every job prompt gets a mandatory finish protocol appended: code review, security review, verify with the project's own checks, commit, then emit a SCHEDULER_VERDICT PASS/FAIL line. A job that exits with uncommitted changes is flagged for review (src/main/scheduler.cjs:274-278, 322-372)

needs_review has a six-rung recovery ladder: mechanical-recovery, resume-recovery, quarantine, auto-fix, reverify, manual-reset (src/main/lib/needsReviewLedger.cjs:34-41; session-manager-operations/architecture/scheduler-operations.md:102-119)

After 30 minutes parked, a needs_review row gets up to 2 automatic requeues and is then auto-skipped, so a dependsOn chain behind it can still drain (src/main/scheduler.cjs:10500-10503; session-manager-operations/architecture/scheduler-operations.md:119)

The auto-fix rung launches a fresh-context `claude -p` that writes a fix PRD, capped at 1 concurrent investigation machine-wide (src/main/scheduler.cjs:3586-3588; session-manager-operations/architecture/scheduler-operations.md:117)

A starvation watchdog runs every 60s and forces a tick if ready work has sat idle for more than 10 minutes (src/main/scheduler.cjs:8662, 8937; session-manager-operations/architecture/scheduler-operations.md:96-100)

A wall-clock budget kills overrunning jobs at clamp(estimate × 3, 45 min, 180 min) and parks them as needs_review, with a 4h hard deadman behind that (src/main/lib/schedulerConfig.cjs:48, 132-134; src/main/scheduler.cjs:2227-2234)

The Scheduler screen has four views, Queue, PRDs, History and Machine, and the Queue view shows plans as Graph, List or Critical path (src/renderer/components/tabs/Scheduler.tsx:30-36, 109-115; src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/SchedulerTopBands.tsx:499)
The title band has Refresh, Pause/Resume and 'Fire next batch' buttons. Pause stops new dispatch without killing running jobs (src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/SchedulerTopBands.tsx:333-354)

The KPI band has six cells: Window used (with 'resets in'), Slots (in use/total), Ready now, Needs you (or 'all clear'), Done today (avg minutes plus spend), and Concurrency (src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/SchedulerTopBands.tsx:361-430)
Plan bands are badged ACTIVE / QUEUED / DONE / DRAFT, with actions Pause plan / Run now / View run / Schedule… (src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/PlanBand.tsx:26-29, 143-180)

Stage-level Retry #N resets a failed job. Review #N opens the authoring Epic, because a parked needs_review job is a question routed back to its session (src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/StageColumn.tsx:58, 141, 153; src/renderer/components/tabs/scheduler/CONTROL_MAP.md:72-73)
The Scheduler nav row is labelled 'Scheduler', with the hint 'This project's live PRD queue + scheduler policy' (src/renderer/lib/navGroups.ts:63)

/develop turns a request into self-contained PRDs sized as <10-minute Sonnet-executable work items (several independent ones, or a 3-5 PRD chain), queues them, tracks them to completion and verifies them against acceptance criteria (plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/SKILL.md:3-10)

/develop's stated rationale is model economics: keep the expensive interactive planner session on decisions and let a cheaper executor model implement as a headless `claude -p` job (plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/SKILL.md:56-60)
PRDs are authored through the `scheduler_create_prd` MCP tool, which validates frontmatter and requires an existing, human-approved Epic (src/main/lib/mcpToolCatalog.cjs:78-90)

Night-shift collage: a moon cut from butter-yellow paper, a sleeping laptop with a taped-on 'do not disturb' sign, and tiny workers still hammering away

doNotClaim: Do NOT say jobs run in a secure sandbox or ask for permissions: they run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Worktrees are git isolation, not a security sandbox (src/main/scheduler.cjs:5444)
